methodological_rigor.justification: In vitro cell culture study with appropriate controls and replicate experiments. Standard molecular biology methods (transfection, reporter assays, western blotting). Statistical analysis uses standard tests (t-tests, ANOVA). Limited sample information provided; no explicit statement of n values or sample size justification. No pre-specification of hypotheses. Methods appear sound but documentation incomplete.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical cell-based mechanistic study investigating miR-21 targeting for HBV-HCC sorafenib sensitization. Study addresses mechanistic question in vitro without animal models or patient validation. Therapeutic strategy has potential but highly preliminary. No clinical translation demonstrated.

reporting_quality.justification: Basic methods described but lacking detail for some elements (cell line sources, culture conditions incomplete). ARRIVE adherence minimal (no animal protocol registration, no data availability statement). Statistical methods sparse; confidence intervals and effect sizes incompletely reported. Reproducibility limited without additional protocol detail.

novelty_literature.justification: Demonstrates that miR-21 inhibition can restore SASH1 expression and enhance sorafenib sensitivity in HBV-HCC cells. Mechanistic contribution is meaningful but builds directly on known miR-21 biology. Novel pathway interaction identified but in limited disease context.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is clearly organized with logical flow from background through results. Figures effectively communicate molecular findings. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings. However, methods section lacks some detail needed for reproducibility. Writing is adequate but not exceptional.

key_strengths: Mechanistic demonstration of miR-21/SASH1 axis in sorafenib resistance using multiple cell-based approaches
Clear identification of functional pathway with potential therapeutic target
Appropriate molecular biology techniques and controls
key_concerns: Preclinical only; in vitro cell models lack physiological complexity and tumor microenvironment
No animal models or patient sample validation
Statistical reporting incomplete; sample sizes and replication details insufficiently documented
Clinical translation pathway unclear and not demonstrated
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent preclinical mechanistic study suitable for specialist journals but lacking validation in more complex systems. Appropriate for Tier 4 with major revisions: requires animal model validation and increased statistical rigor in reporting.
